title: The Acts Of The Apostles & Foundation Through Christ

sense.text:
“Ye are the children of the prophets, and of the covenant which God made with our fathers, saying unto Abraham, And in thy seed shall all the kindreds of the earth be blessed.” Through Abraham’s seed shall all the kindreds of the earth be blessed.

But who are these children? To understand who the children are in the third chapter of Acts, we need to know who the prophets are. The prophets were raised up out of the sons of Israel, so this is talking to the children of Israel.

“Unto you first God, having raised up his Son Jesus, sent him to bless you, in turning away every one of you from his iniquities.” Who’s the you? The children of the prophets, Israel. Christ was sent to bless them and to turn every one of them away from his iniquities.

Before we can get back to the book of Acts, we need the foundation: a fundamental basis, a solid foundation, so we can connect all of the dots.

precepts.why:
“And I raised up of your sons for prophets, and of your young men for Nazarites. Is it not even thus, O ye children of Israel?” O ye children of who? Of Israel.

The prophets were raised up out of Israel’s own sons. So when Acts 3:25 says “Ye are the children of the prophets”, we understand who it is talking to: the children of Israel.

sense.text:
“For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ.” Our foundation is not of our own works, not of our own opinions, emotions or feelings. It always has to go back to Messiah, our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ.

That is the whole point of the acts of the apostles and the foundation through Christ: before we read the book of Acts, we lay the foundation, why Christ came and what he did.

“Now therefore ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of God”. Now you are fellowcitizens with the saints. So that means something had to happen aforetime in order for you to become fellowcitizens with the saints. Weren’t you already a fellow citizen?

The saints are the children of Israel, God’s people. When the kingdom was rent in two, the northern kingdom, Israel and Ephraim, became strangers over time. That is what the scripture is letting you know: the strangers and foreigners here had to be Israelites.

So when it gets to the New Testament, the northern kingdom of Israel is back in the fold. They are now fellowcitizens with the rest of the saints. All throughout the scriptures it says the same thing, so why does mainstream Christianity act as if the book of Acts is something totally different?

“And are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone”. Remember, we are going over the acts of the apostles and the foundation through Christ. The chief corner stone is Christ, the leader; then you had the apostles that followed Christ.

So when you get to the acts of the apostles, they are not teaching something different than Christ. They are carrying on the same exact doctrine.

precepts.why:
Who are the saints according to the scriptures? “He also exalteth the horn of his people, the praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel”. That horn is the foundation, Jesus the Christ, and it is going into rulership.

The only people that can be saints are the children of Israel. So the saints of Ephesians 2:19 are Israel.

Remember, Christ comes in the volume of the book. Christ was sent for the nation of Israel, his people, because we were cut off from that inheritance. He came to bring us back to the fold. It’s that simple.

Psalms also mentions his people: “Hear, O my people, and I will testify unto thee: O Israel, if thou wilt hearken unto me”.

This ain’t talking to everybody else. It is talking to God’s people, only you, not all. The Lord is letting us know that his people are the Israelites.

Something had to happen for Israel to become strangers. “Wherefore the Lord said unto Solomon, Forasmuch as this is done of thee, and thou hast not kept my covenant and my statutes, which I have commanded thee, I will surely rend the kingdom from thee, and will give it to thy servant.”

To rend is to split or tear apart or in pieces by violence. Because of Solomon’s sin, his transgression, the kingdom of Israel would be rent, split into two. The southern kingdom remained with King Solomon, and the northern kingdom was taken. When you read the scriptures, the northern kingdom is called Israel and Ephraim.

That is how the Israelites of the northern kingdom became strangers over time. So when Ephesians 2:19 says “ye are no more strangers and foreigners”, it is talking about them coming back.

Before we can understand the kingdom being rent, we need to know what kingdom he is talking about. David says the Lord “hath chosen Solomon my son to sit upon the throne of the kingdom of the Lord over Israel.”

The kingdom over who? Over Israel. So when it talks about the kingdom being rent, it is talking about the kingdom of Israel, one joint kingdom, split in two.

The apostles carry on the same doctrine as Christ. “Jesus answered them, and said, My doctrine is not mine, but his that sent me.” Christ lets them know his doctrine is not his own, but the Father’s that sent him.

“If any man will do his will, he shall know of the doctrine”. If you keep God’s commandments, you are going to know of the doctrine. The present-day Christian church does not do his will. You get understanding by keeping God’s commandments, and you get the Holy Spirit by keeping God’s commandments.

You’re not going to understand the mysteries of this Bible if you’re shaving your beard, forsaking the Sabbath day and treating the first day of the week as the Sabbath, sisters wearing pants, brothers not wearing fringes, worshipping and crying to a white man as your saviour. You have to keep God’s commandments to understand the doctrine of Christ, which is not his own, but the Father’s.

Why was Christ sent to the earth? “I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.”

The Father sent Christ to redeem the lost sheep of the house of Israel. That wasn’t his decision; that was the Father’s decision. That is the doctrine the apostles were built upon.

You have to go to the scriptures, to the precepts, to show it. We’re not making any of this up. “I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.”

To fulfil God’s will, you have to keep his laws, statutes and commandments. Those that don’t keep God’s commandments are not going to understand the Bible like the Israelites understand the Bible.

“And they continued stedfastly in the apostles’ doctrine and fellowship”. They are the apostles, and the apostles are the disciples. The disciples rode with Christ, so who taught them the doctrine? Jesus Christ.

So when you get to the book of Acts, it is not something different than what Christ taught. That is why we take our time to get the foundation through Christ, to understand why Christ came and what he did.

sense.text:
Just in case they say we’re isolating or jumping here and there, we read for more context. “Wherefore remember, that ye being in time past Gentiles in the flesh”. We understand the saints are the Israelites. So is this saying another nation can now become an Israelite? Absolutely not. That’s impossible.

You are who you are; you are what your bloodline is. If you grow an apple in America or in China, it’s still an apple. The apple doesn’t have another nationality now. But that’s what Christianity sounds like today when they say spiritual Israel. There’s nowhere in the Bible that can back up that belief.

“Who are called Uncircumcision by that which is called the Circumcision in the flesh made by hands”. The Circumcision is the southern kingdom, the Jews. They referred to the northern kingdom as the Uncircumcision, because they were cut off. They went to idolatry, as the prophecy said when the kingdom was rent in two.

“That at that time ye were without Christ”. You were in idolatry, serving the gods of the nations. Just like Christianity today, where you have black men attacking their black brothers with vicious attacks daily on social media. But when Charlie Brown or Chucky, whoever his name is, the oppressor, passes away, the one who blatantly says black people are not as intelligent, who says he doesn’t feel comfortable with a black pilot up there, who says Christianity is only for white people, you burst out into tears. Yet you’re busy attacking your own brothers.

“Being aliens from the commonwealth of Israel”. Commonwealth is going into community: a nation of people, housing, cities together, pooling your resources together. That community is the Israelite community. Being aliens from it shows you that you were once a part of that community.

“And strangers from the covenants of promise, having no hope, and without God in the world”. Hold on to that word strangers.

“But now in Christ Jesus ye who sometimes were far off are made nigh by the blood of Christ.” Who’s the ye, the ones who were far off? The Israelites, Jacob, saved from afar off. Paul is letting you know exactly who his audience is. It’s just that your oppressors have taught you another gospel, which in fact is not another gospel.

Now you can come close. You can come back into the community, the commonwealth with the saints, through Jesus Christ.

“For he is our peace”. Our is possessive. Christ is the Israelites’ peace.

“Who hath made both one”. Two is the same thing as both. It was one joint kingdom, then it was rent in two, and now there are no longer two nations but one united nation under Christ.

“And hath broken down the middle wall of partition between us”. What was against us was the law of sacrifice. No more is that division going to cut us off. Now we can get back on the good side of our Father through Jesus Christ.

precepts.why:
It is all talking about the same people. “But fear not thou, O my servant Jacob, and be not dismayed, O Israel: for, behold, I will save thee from afar off, and thy seed from the land of their captivity”.

I will save who? Thee. That thee is Jacob, Israel; remember Jacob’s name was changed to Israel. So the ones “far off” in Ephesians 2:13 are Israel in the land of their captivity.

Who hath made both one? “Behold, I will take the children of Israel from among the heathen, whither they be gone, and will gather them on every side, and bring them into their own land: And I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Israel; and one king shall be king to them all: and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all”.

Two nations. Two is the same thing as both; both is talking about two. It was one joint kingdom, but the kingdom was rent in two, and here God says they will never be divided into two kingdoms any more at all.

Jump to verse 27: “My tabernacle also shall be with them: yea, I will be their God, and they shall be my people.” Who’s that? Both nations, Israel. Then: “And the heathen shall know that I the Lord do sanctify Israel, when my sanctuary shall be in the midst of them for evermore.”

You see the difference right there? The heathen ain’t included in that. There is a stellar difference between the both and the heathen. So why are you trying to include them in Acts? Why are you trying to include them in Ephesians?

He is our peace. “Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.”

Christ leaves peace with you: his audience, the twelve and the Israelites. And when Christ ascended up, he sent the Comforter, the Holy Ghost, the Holy Spirit.

sense.text: “When at the first he lightly afflicted the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, and afterward did more grievously afflict her by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, in Galilee of the nations.” Zebulun and Naphtali are two tribes in the northern kingdom of Israel. They would be afflicted and walking in darkness, because they went to idolatry: they were afflicted because of their sin, their transgression.

“The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light”. That great light is Christ, the life that is the light of men.

“They that dwell in the land of the shadow of death”. That is going into captivity: we would be scattered according to the prophecy. The shadow of death is going into slavery.

“Upon them hath the light shined.” That’s Christ coming to the prisoners, the captives. He’s that light. Everybody’s not captives. When you have captives, you have captors; you have the oppressed and you have the oppressors. That’s not everybody. That’s talking about one particular nation: Zebulun and Naphtali, Israelites.

“For thou hast broken the yoke of his burden, and the staff of his shoulder, the rod of his oppressor, as in the day of Midian.” The rod of his oppressor: that is how you know this is talking about the Israelites being scattered and made captives.
“But this shall be with burning and fuel of fire.” Our salvation is going to be with burning and fuel of fire, just like Christ said in Matthew 3.

“For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given”. Who’s the us? Zebulun and Naphtali, the Israelites.

“And his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God”. Christ is referred to as the mighty God. “The Prince of Peace.” Ain’t that what Ephesians 2:14 said, he is our peace? Who’s the our? Both nations, Judah and Israel. All you have to do is read.

“Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end”. Remember, world without end. The other nations, they’ve got an end. But that world without end is God’s people, because once Christ reigns, it’s going to be forever: “upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom, to order it, and to establish it with judgment and with justice from henceforth even for ever.”

“The Lord sent a word into Jacob, and it hath lighted upon Israel.” Just in case you were confused, this word was sent to Jacob, and it has lighted upon Israel. The scriptures talk about a light unto the Gentiles; I wonder what that’s talking about.

precepts.why:
The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light. “In him was life; and the life was the light of men.”

Christ is that great light that shined upon Zebulun and Naphtali in the land of the shadow of death.

Who was Deuteronomy written to, just in case someone is mistaken? “These be the words which Moses spake unto all Israel on this side Jordan in the wilderness”.

So the scattering prophesied in Deuteronomy is spoken to all Israel.

They that dwell in the land of the shadow of death are going into captivity: we would be scattered according to the prophecy. “And the Lord shall scatter you among the nations, and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen”.

Scattered amongst the heathen. The shadow of death is going into slavery, and that is where Israel was dwelling when the great light shined upon them.

“Then said I, Lo, I come: in the volume of the book it is written of me”. The child born unto us in Isaiah 9, that was Christ right there.

He comes in the volume of the book: it is written of him all throughout. So we have to go and find out the foundation of Christ, to see what he is talking about the whole time and why he was sent.

sense.text: “Jesus himself drew near, and went with them. But their eyes were holden that they should not know him.” This is when Christ rose and presented himself. They didn’t know that was him, because he made it to the point where they couldn’t recognize him.

“What manner of communications are these that ye have one to another, as ye walk, and are sad?” They were sad. They told him “Concerning Jesus of Nazareth, which was a prophet mighty in deed and word before God and all the people” and how the chief priests and rulers “have crucified him.”

“But we trusted that it had been he which should have redeemed Israel”. Christ died, and they don’t know that’s Christ in the midst of them, risen again. They’re saying, we’re sad, because we really thought he was going to be the redeemer of Israel. I wonder where they got that from? From Ezekiel 37, from the ninth chapter of Isaiah. They read the prophecy.

So was there any confusion amongst the Israelites about who Christ came to redeem? No. What are we reading? The New Testament. There was no confusion.

“And beside all this, to day is the third day since these things were done.” They understood Christ said he would rise again the third day. They thought it didn’t happen, and they were bummed out, because they were ready to be redeemed.

precepts.why:
So where does confusion come from today? “For God is not the author of confusion, but of peace, as in all churches of the saints.”

Remember, he’s our peace. But anytime we start joining together, anytime we start unifying, the other nations come to tear it up. Who do they really hate? They hate our peace. They hate Christ.

How in the world do you unite thousands of blacks and Hispanics and no violence breaks out, no murder, everybody in joy and peace? The only way you could do that is through the spirit of Christ, and they want to break that up.

sense.text: “Behold my servant, whom I uphold; mine elect, in whom my soul delighteth; I have put my spirit upon him: he shall bring forth judgment to the Gentiles.”

“He shall not cry, nor lift up, nor cause his voice to be heard in the street.” When Christ came, he was not there to argue. He got the doctrine straight from the Father, and he understood why he came. The Pharisees were trying to argue with him and catch him in his words. Christ didn’t come for that.

“A bruised reed shall he not break”. That is referring to the northern kingdom. “And the smoking flax shall he not quench”: he’s not going to quench their spirit.

“He shall bring forth judgment unto truth.” He’s going to teach the laws. Remember, he’s coming to bring judgment to the Gentiles. Why? Because they’ve been captives, and he’s going to bring salvation to them.
“He shall not fail nor be discouraged, till he have set judgment in the earth: and the isles shall wait for his law.”

Pay close attention: “I the Lord have called thee in righteousness, and will hold thine hand, and will keep thee, and give thee for a covenant of the people, for a light of the Gentiles”. Christians would say that’s all nations right there, because they don’t read the Old Testament. That’s not talking about nobody else except the Israelites.

“To open the blind eyes, to bring out the prisoners from the prison, and them that sit in darkness out of the prison house.” From the prisons, the shadow of death. That is who the light of the Gentiles comes for.

precepts.why:
“He shall not strive, nor cry; neither shall any man hear his voice in the streets.”

Matthew shows Christ fulfilling Isaiah 42. He did not come to argue in the streets with those trying to catch him in his words; he came with the Father’s doctrine, knowing why he was sent.

“The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim”. Didn’t we read about the land of Zebulun just a few moments ago, in the ninth chapter of Isaiah? When Christ came on the scene, he came and fulfilled exactly what was written of him.

“By the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles”. Galilee of who? Of the Gentiles. The Bible is letting you know in the New Testament that the Gentiles are Israelites. Yes, the Gentiles are Israelites.

“The people which sat in darkness saw great light”. So the “light of the Gentiles” in Isaiah 42:6 is the light that shined on Zebulun and Naphtali: Israel.

“The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives”. To the captives.

“And recovering of sight to the blind”: remember, Isaiah just said “To open the blind eyes”. “To set at liberty them that are bruised”: the bruised reed of Isaiah 42:3, “A bruised reed shall he not break”. He’s telling you exactly who he came for.

“To preach the acceptable year of the Lord.”

sense.text:
We have to go through the history to get the understanding, so when we get back to Acts 1, Acts 2, or the whole book in itself, we understand what it is talking about. “For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.”

Who’s the we? The Israelites. The Lord knew they were going to come and switch up the doctrine. So we have to read what was written aforetime, so we can get an understanding and so we can learn.

“It is a light thing that thou shouldest be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob”. That’s a redundant statement; we already read multiple examples of what Christ came to do.

“And to restore the preserved of Israel”. Who’s the preserved? The southern kingdom. Remember, the kingdom was rent and split into two.

“I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles”. We read that. Who is that? Zebulun, Naphtali, Ephraim: the northern kingdom of Israel. It’s very simple. “That thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth.”

“Thus saith the Lord, the Redeemer of Israel, and his Holy One”: the Father and the Son.

“To him whom man despiseth, to him whom the nation abhorreth”. They hate our peace. The other nations hate our peace, because Christ came back to unite the twelve tribes of Israel, and they hate to see it.

“And he shall choose thee.” He’s going to choose us.

“Thus saith the Lord, In an acceptable time have I heard thee, and in a day of salvation have I helped thee”. This sounds very familiar. That salvation is for the tribes of Jacob and the preserved of Israel, and Paul brings this same word to the Corinthians.

precepts.why:
“We then, as workers together with him, beseech you also that ye receive not the grace of God in vain.” Paul is talking to the Corinthians. “(For he saith, I have heard thee in a time accepted, and in the day of salvation have I succoured thee: behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation.)”

We just read who that salvation was for in Isaiah 49. Now Paul is hitting the Corinthians with it. This is the fulfilment of that prophecy, so the Corinthians have to be those same people in Isaiah 49.

Verse 11: “O ye Corinthians, our mouth is open unto you”. That prophecy was talking about you, showing you that the Corinthians have to be Israelites.

The Corinthians have to be Israel. “After these things Paul departed from Athens, and came to Corinth; And found a certain Jew named Aquila”.

Paul came to Corinth and found a certain Jew. The Israelites were in Corinth.

“Moreover, brethren, I would not that ye should be ignorant, how that all our fathers were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea; And were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea”. Paul tells the Corinthians that their fathers were under the cloud.

“And did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.” Christ, who is our foundation.

So the Corinthians Paul brought Isaiah 49:8 to are the children of the fathers who passed through the sea: Israel.

What is Paul referring to with the cloud? “And the Lord went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud, to lead them the way; and by night in a pillar of fire, to give them light”.

Who’s the them? The Israelites. That was the Lord leading Israel throughout the wilderness. So when Paul tells the Corinthians “our fathers were under the cloud”, their fathers are Israel.

sense.text:
“Then shalt thou say in thine heart, Who hath begotten me these, seeing I have lost my children, and am desolate, a captive, and removing to and fro?” The I is Jerusalem, the land, talking about her children, the children of Israel. The Israelites left and the Gentiles inhabit the land. Desolate, a captive, removing to and fro: scattered throughout the whole earth.

“Behold, I was left alone; these, where had they been?” Jerusalem is crying out, where are my children? Where are the Israelites? These other nations ain’t them. That shows you what this spiritual Israel stuff they talk about is.

“Thus saith the Lord God, Behold, I will lift up mine hand to the Gentiles, and set up my standard to the people: and they shall bring thy sons in their arms, and thy daughters shall be carried upon their shoulders.”

If the Gentiles of verse 6 are the other nations, who is this in verse 22? If you’re the sons, how are you also the ones bringing the sons? These are two different Gentiles. The Gentiles in verse 6, “a light to the Gentiles”, are Israelites. The Gentiles in verse 22 are the actual Gentile nations outside of Israel, who are going to bring the sons and daughters of the Israelites to the land. That’s called understanding.

“And kings shall be thy nursing fathers, and their queens thy nursing mothers”. The kings of the other nations are going to be our nursing fathers. “They shall bow down to thee with their face toward the earth, and lick up the dust of thy feet”.

“For they shall not be ashamed that wait for me.” Who’s not going to be ashamed? The world without end. It’s not talking about everybody.

“Even the captives of the mighty shall be taken away, and the prey of the terrible shall be delivered”. We’re the prey of the terrible. The Lord is letting us know we are going to be delivered through our Lord and Saviour, our foundation, which is in Christ Jesus.

“For I will contend with him that contendeth with thee, and I will save thy children.” Everybody that wanted to contend with us, mess with us and hinder us, the Lord is now going to contend with you.

“And I will feed them that oppress thee with their own flesh; and they shall be drunken with their own blood, as with sweet wine”. The Lord is going to feed those who oppress the children of Israel with their own flesh.

“And all flesh shall know that I the Lord am thy Saviour and thy Redeemer, the mighty One of Jacob.” It’s very simple: he’s the redeemer of Israel. To redeem is to buy back, to get or win back, to repurchase. If you buy something back, that means you possessed it before. Who did the Lord possess before? His people. So the Lord is going to buy back his people from the other nations.

“Keep ye judgment, and do justice: for my salvation is near to come, and my righteousness to be revealed.” He revealed it: when you get to the Gospels and the book of Acts, that’s Christ’s righteousness being revealed.

“Blessed is the man that doeth this, and the son of man that layeth hold on it; that keepeth the sabbath from polluting it, and keepeth his hand from doing any evil.” When Christ comes on the scene, you better be keeping his commandments.

“Neither let the son of the stranger, that hath joined himself to the Lord, speak, saying, The Lord hath utterly separated me from his people”. Didn’t we read about that stranger earlier in Ephesians 2? Is this talking about someone of another nation? Now you’re starting to see it’s probably talking about Israel some way.

“Neither let the eunuch say, Behold, I am a dry tree.” Under the law of sacrifice, the blemished and the eunuch could not come near. In that day when Christ comes, it doesn’t matter anymore for everybody of the seed: no longer by the law of sacrifice, but through Christ, through the spirit. The eunuch is going to be accepted in that day too.

“Also the sons of the stranger, that join themselves to the Lord, to serve him, and to love the name of the Lord, to be his servants, every one that keepeth the sabbath from polluting it, and taketh hold of my covenant”. We have to deal with the stranger, because they say that’s the other nations right there. No. There are a lot of ways to prove that the Israelites are the strangers according to the prophecy, like the Israelite strangers in Leviticus 25.

“Even them will I bring to my holy mountain, and make them joyful in my house of prayer: their burnt offerings and their sacrifices shall be accepted upon mine altar; for mine house shall be called an house of prayer for all people.” Boy, do they love using this scripture. They say it’s talking about all nations, kindreds and tongues.

But no other people are going to be ruling in the coming kingdom. When it says an house of prayer for all people, that’s talking about all people of Israel.

“The Lord God which gathereth the outcasts of Israel saith, Yet will I gather others to him, beside those that are gathered unto him.” Here they come: tag me in, we can get in. Wrong. The outcasts of Israel are gathered, and the others gathered to him are the dispersed of Judah, gathered from the four corners of the earth.

precepts.why:
What is the eunuch going into? “Speak unto Aaron, saying, Whosoever he be of thy seed in their generations that hath any blemish, let him not approach to offer the bread of his God.” Of thy seed: the seed of Israel.

“For whatsoever man he be that hath a blemish, he shall not approach: a blind man, or a lame, or he that hath a flat nose”, down to the one that “hath his stones broken”. His stones broken: this is going into the balls.

Leviticus 21 is going into the law of sacrifice. In that day under Christ, it would no longer be the law of sacrifice; it would be through Christ, through the spirit. So the eunuch of Isaiah 56:3 is not left out.

“He that is wounded in the stones, or hath his privy member cut off, shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord.”

That is the eunuch who says “Behold, I am a dry tree.” Under the law he was shut out of the congregation; when Christ comes, he is accepted in that day too.

We’re dealing with that stranger in Isaiah 56:6. “Then fled Moses at this saying, and was a stranger in the land of Madian”.

Moses, an Israelite, was a stranger. There are a lot of ways to prove that the Israelites are the strangers according to the prophecy.

“And he gathered all Judah and Benjamin, and the strangers with them out of Ephraim and Manasseh, and out of Simeon”.

The strangers came out of Ephraim, out of the northern kingdom, and Manasseh and Simeon. So these strangers it’s talking about are Israelites, and so are “the sons of the stranger” of Isaiah 56:6.

Mine house shall be called an house of prayer for all people? Please explain this scripture: “And in the days of these kings”. That’s going into the powers that be right now: Trump, Macron, all of these other kings, Bibi and them.

“Shall the God of heaven set up a kingdom, which shall never be destroyed”. You’ve got ruling kingdoms right now, but the Lord is letting it be known prophetically that while these powerful kingdoms are ruling, there is going to be another kingdom that the Lord is going to put his spirit on in the midst of their rulership.

“And the kingdom shall not be left to other people”. This kingdom shall not be left to other people. So when it says “mine house shall be called an house of prayer for all people”, that is talking about all people of Israel, because no other people are going to be ruling in this coming kingdom.

Let’s figure out who the others are. “The Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people, which shall be left, from Assyria, and from Egypt, and from Pathros, and from Cush, and from Elam, and from Shinar, and from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea.”

Remember, this is the foundation through Christ. This is what the book of Acts is about: recovering his people from these lands that we’ve been scattered to.

“And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.” The outcasts of Israel, just as Isaiah 56:8 said, and the dispersed of Judah: these are the others he is going to gather to him. From the four corners of the earth, because we’ve been scattered throughout the four corners of the earth.

sense.text:
Now we examine Christ’s example and his message in the Gospels before he was killed. “Then said the Jews among themselves, Whither will he go, that we shall not find him? will he go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles, and teach the Gentiles?”

The dispersed: didn’t we just read about the dispersed in Isaiah 11? The dispersed Israelites amongst the Gentiles. And the dispersed amongst the Gentiles were called Gentiles. This is Christ’s message right here.
“He left Judea, and departed again into Galilee. And he must needs go through Samaria.” Christ came through Samaria. So let’s figure out who lives in Samaria: Ephraim, the northern kingdom.
“Then cometh he to a city of Samaria, which is called Sychar, near to the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph. Now Jacob’s well was there.”

Who’s the her? The Samaritan woman. “If thou knewest the gift of God, and who it is that saith to thee, Give me to drink; thou wouldest have asked of him, and he would have given thee living water.” Christ has to be talking about something that was written aforetime. If you knew who you were talking to, you would be asking the right questions.

“Art thou greater than our father Jacob”. She had to know something. She knew she’s an Israelite, and she knew Christ was from the southern kingdom, and she knew they both had the same daddy, Jacob, whose name was changed to Israel.

It’s very plain what Christ was doing before he was crucified.

precepts.why:
Who lives in Samaria? “Within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken, that it be not a people. And the head of Ephraim is Samaria”.

Ephraim is a representation of the northern kingdom, and they dwelt in Samaria. So when Christ “must needs go through Samaria”, he went to the northern kingdom of Israel.

“O Lord, the hope of Israel”. Our Lord is only the hope of Israel. “All that forsake thee shall be ashamed, and they that depart from me shall be written in the earth, because they have forsaken the Lord, the fountain of living waters.”

That’s what Christ was offering the woman of Samaria: the living water, the Lord, the fountain of living waters. That’s why Christ said, if you knew who you were talking to, you would be asking the right questions.

sense.text: Christ knew that he had to come and die in order for both nations, both kingdoms, to be united again and brought back into the fold. “For then must he often have suffered since the foundation of the world: but now once in the end of the world hath he appeared to put away sin by the sacrifice of himself.” Christ put away the sins of Israel by sacrificing himself.

precepts.why:
“For Christ also hath once suffered for sins, the just for the unjust, that he might bring us to God”. To bring us, both the southern and northern kingdom, back to the Father through his death.

“Being put to death in the flesh, but quickened by the Spirit”, when he rose again.

“For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we shall be saved by his life.” By the life of Christ.

To reconcile is to restore. In order to restore, you had to have it before. He never had a relationship with the other nations; his relationship was always with the nation of Israel. So reconciliation is only for Israel.

sense.text: “Ye know that after two days is the feast of the passover, and the Son of man is betrayed to be crucified.” Christ lets it be known that the Passover is coming up, but he also lets you know something else: Christ died on the high holy day of the Passover.

“If thou be Christ, save thyself and us.” The other malefactor rebuked him: “And we indeed justly; for we receive the due reward of our deeds: but this man hath done nothing amiss.” They are saying, we actually committed sin, we deserve to be up here, but Christ didn’t do nothing wrong.

“Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom.” Why would he say that? Because he was following Christ before that. This is not that deathbed confession stuff that you Christians believe in, that I can repent on my deathbed. That’s not what it’s talking about. He followed Christ.

“Verily I say unto thee, To day shalt thou be with me in paradise.”

“And it was about the sixth hour, and there was a darkness over all the earth until the ninth hour.” The sixth hour is noon. If there’s darkness at twelve noon, is that normal? No. Something had to be taking place: a solar eclipse.

On Passover 2024, April the 8th, a solar eclipse took place at the beginning of Passover, showing you that the Bible is a true book. A solar eclipse can only take place fourteen days after a new moon, which also lets you know we have the right understanding on the new moon. Our Lord and Saviour Jesus the Christ was crucified on the Passover.
“And they rose up the same hour, and returned to Jerusalem, and found the eleven gathered together”, saying “The Lord is risen indeed, and hath appeared to Simon.”

Christ stood in their midst and said “Peace be unto you.” They supposed they had seen a spirit, and he said “handle me, and see; for a spirit hath not flesh and bones, as ye see me have.” Then he took the broiled fish and honeycomb “and did eat before them.”

“That all things must be fulfilled, which were written in the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms, concerning me.” Christ is amongst the twelve, letting them know: this is everything that was written of me, and it’s coming to pass.
“Then opened he their understanding, that they might understand the scriptures”. Then they understood. They started connecting the dots with all the prophecies.
“Thus it behoved Christ to suffer, and to rise from the dead the third day”. Three days after the Passover.
“And that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name among all nations, beginning at Jerusalem.” Amongst all nations. I wonder why? Because Israel is scattered in all nations.

“But tarry ye in the city of Jerusalem, until ye be endued with power from on high.” We want to focus on that: stay in Jerusalem until you are endued with power from on high. What is he talking about? The book of Acts picks it up.

“The former treatise have I made, O Theophilus, of all that Jesus began both to do and teach”. Luke is the one who was with Paul on his journeys, and he wrote Acts. The former treatise is the book of Luke, written to the same Theophilus.

“To whom also he shewed himself alive after his passion by many infallible proofs”. We just read this in the twenty-fourth chapter of Luke. Acts picks up from the end of Luke; it is a continuation of Luke 24.

“Being seen of them forty days”. Christ rose three days after the Passover, then stayed on the earth forty more days: forty-three days after the Passover.

“And speaking of the things pertaining to the kingdom of God”, which belongs to the Israelites.

“And, being assembled together with them, commanded them that they should not depart from Jerusalem, but wait for the promise of the Father, which, saith he, ye have heard of me.” This is the tarrying in Jerusalem from the end of Luke.

“For John truly baptized with water; but ye shall be baptized with the Holy Ghost not many days hence.” Three days after the Passover he rose, and he presented himself forty more days: forty-three. So when he says not many days hence, he is saying, in just a few more days, you know what’s coming up? Pentecost, fifty days after the Passover.

Penta means fifty. But it’s really the feast of first fruits.

precepts.why:
We need to find out a little bit about Luke. “It seemed good to me also, having had perfect understanding of all things from the very first, to write unto thee in order, most excellent Theophilus”.

Most excellent Theophilus: one of the companions Luke addressed, both in the book of Luke and in the book of Acts. So the same man wrote both.

Luke accompanied Paul the Apostle during his travels. “Luke, the beloved physician, and Demas, greet you.”

This is Paul writing to the church at Colosse. How would he know Luke greets them? Luke was with him.

“Only Luke is with me. Take Mark, and bring him with thee: for he is profitable to me for the ministry.”

Do you think Paul the Apostle is going to take just anybody with him in his travels? Christians teach that Luke was of another nation. No, he wasn’t. Paul is not going to have someone of another nation with him; that is against the doctrine of Christ.

In literature and other texts, Luke is said to be one of the seventy. “After these things the Lord appointed other seventy also, and sent them two and two before his face into every city and place, whither he himself would come.”

Other seventy also: there were more disciples outside of the twelve, and Luke was one of them.

Pentecost is fifty days after the Passover. “In the fourteenth day of the first month at even is the Lord’s passover. And on the fifteenth day of the same month is the feast of unleavened bread”.

Jump down to verse 15: “And ye shall count unto you from the morrow after the sabbath, from the day that ye brought the sheaf of the wave offering; seven sabbaths shall be complete”. Count seven sabbaths and that gives you forty-nine days from the Passover. “Even unto the morrow after the seventh sabbath shall ye number fifty days”. After the seventh sabbath, that sundown is the fiftieth day.

“And ye shall offer a new meat offering unto the Lord.” The two wave loaves “are the firstfruits unto the Lord.” So the “not many days hence” of Acts 1:5 is the day of Pentecost, the feast of first fruits.

This goes with what was written in Isaiah 56 about keeping his sabbaths. “If ye love me, keep my commandments.”

“And I will pray the Father, and he shall give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever”. You have to keep the commandments in order for the Comforter, the Holy Spirit, to be sent. That is the baptism with the Holy Ghost promised in Acts 1:5.

“But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you.”

“Peace I leave with you”. You see that? Peace he leaves with us. Remember, Christ is our peace.

sense.text: “Lord, wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel?” Remember what we read in Luke 24: they thought Christ was going to be the one to redeem Israel. Christ told them to wait for him in Jerusalem, and now he is speaking with them, and they’re asking, is this the time? Are we going to get the kingdom now?

“It is not for you to know the times or the seasons, which the Father hath put in his own power. But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you”. He already alluded that the feast of Pentecost is right around the corner: don’t worry, I’m still going to be with you until I make my return.

“And ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judea, and in Samaria”. I wonder why he mentioned Samaria? Because the Israelites are in Samaria. Go to Jerusalem, all Judea, Samaria first, then to all the rest of the scattered: “unto the uttermost part of the earth.”
“He was taken up; and a cloud received him out of their sight.” That chariot received Christ out of their sight.

“This same Jesus, which is taken up from you into heaven, shall so come in like manner as ye have seen him go into heaven.” Christ is going to make his return, to bring judgment, and then the kingdom of heaven is going to appear.

They returned to Jerusalem into an upper room, and “These all continued with one accord in prayer and supplication”. After Christ ascended up to be with the Father, they continued to fellowship and congregate amongst one another.

precepts.why:
“He added and spake a parable, because he was nigh to Jerusalem, and because they thought that the kingdom of God should immediately appear.”

That’s what they were thinking. Our forefathers understood the prophecy, so they thought as soon as Messiah was there, the kingdom was just going to appear. That’s the mindset we were in when they asked, “wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel?”

sense.text: “And when the day of Pentecost was fully come, they were all with one accord in one place.” The not many days hence was the feast of Pentecost, the fiftieth day. Remember, Christ isn’t on the earth at this point; he’s with the Father.

“And suddenly there came a sound from heaven as of a rushing mighty wind, and it filled all the house where they were sitting.” Cloven tongues like as of fire sat upon each of them, “And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost”. This is during the feast of first fruits.

precepts.why:
“For as in Adam all die, even so in Christ shall all be made alive.” Remember, he’s the life, the light of men. Through Christ, the second Adam, do we all live.

“But every man in his own order: Christ the firstfruits; afterward they that are Christ’s at his coming.” We were cut off, without hope in the world, but now we’ve got a chance at life again through Christ.

Christ stuck around forty more days so he could fulfil that prophecy. Christ is that offering, that sacrifice; he’s the first fruits. And on the fiftieth day, he poured out his spirit upon all flesh.

“Be glad then, ye children of Zion, and rejoice in the Lord your God: for he hath given you the former rain moderately, and he will cause to come down for you the rain, the former rain, and the latter rain in the first month.” That rain provides moisture for crops. And what high holy day is in the first month? The Passover.

“And the floors shall be full of wheat, and the fats shall overflow with wine and oil. And I will restore to you the years that the locust hath eaten”. The locust eats up the crops. “My great army which I sent among you”: this is multifold. That great army is talking about the northern army, and about what’s to come as well.

“And ye shall eat in plenty, and be satisfied”. He’s going to give us that rain so our crops can grow; that’s what the feast of first fruits is about. “And ye shall know that I am in the midst of Israel, and that I am the Lord your God, and none else: and my people shall never be ashamed.” He’s the Lord God of Israel and none else. He’s going to reconcile, he’s going to restore all things.

“And it shall come to pass afterward, that I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh”. The Lord poured out his spirit upon all flesh during Pentecost, the feast of first fruits. This is talking about Acts 2, and it is also talking about our redemption to come.

sense.text:
“And there were dwelling at Jerusalem Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven.” Out of every nation, because the Israelites were scattered in every nation. Why is everybody coming together? Because they’re coming together to keep the commandment.

This class is your prerequisite for the book of Acts. Christians, before you read it, watch this class first so you can understand what you read.
“Every man heard them speak in his own language.” “Behold, are not all these which speak Galileans? And how hear we every man in our own tongue, wherein we were born?”

Parthians, Medes, Elamites, the dwellers in Mesopotamia, Judea, Cappadocia, Pontus and Asia, Phrygia, Pamphylia, Egypt, Libya, “and strangers of Rome”. We understand those strangers are not Caucasians. Those strangers are Israelites living in Rome.

That’s why we had to go get the foundation through Christ, so we can understand what the apostles were preaching in the book of Acts.

precepts.why:
Why is everybody coming together? “Three times in a year shall all thy males appear before the Lord thy God in the place which he shall choose; in the feast of unleavened bread, and in the feast of weeks, and in the feast of tabernacles”.

The feast of weeks is going into counting seven sabbaths: the feast of weeks, first fruits, Pentecost. This is a commandment. No matter where you’re at, you’ve got to come to Jerusalem.

That is why Christ said tarry in Jerusalem until you receive power from on high. Christ wasn’t going to be there anymore. Yes, he had the twelve; yes, he had the seventy. But in order to spread the gospel throughout the whole earth, the spirit had to be poured on everybody. Everybody was going to come to Jerusalem for the feast, so the Holy Spirit could be dispersed upon all Israel, and they could go back and teach the gospel to the four corners.

sense.text: “And it shall come to pass afterward, that I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh; and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, your old men shall dream dreams, your young men shall see visions”. Remember, this is prophetic of Acts 2 and of what’s to come.

“And I will shew wonders in the heavens and in the earth, blood, and fire, and pillars of smoke.” Pillars of smoke: this is going into those nukes, those bombs. The sky is going to be flooded with smoke; it’s going to be dark and gloomy, because war is going on. “The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the great and the terrible day of the Lord come.”

“And it shall come to pass, that whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be delivered: for in mount Zion and in Jerusalem shall be deliverance”. He already said he is “the Lord your God, and none else”, the Lord God of Israel. Whosoever ain’t talking about just anybody. That’s only talking about the nation of Israel. Thank the Lord for that; that’s good news right there, that’s the gospel.

“As the Lord hath said, and in the remnant whom the Lord shall call.” Who is the remnant that the Lord shall call?

precepts.why:
Who are God’s called? “Hearken unto me, O Jacob and Israel, my called”.

God’s called are the nation of Israel. So “the remnant whom the Lord shall call” in Joel 2:32 is Israel.

sense.text: “Ye men of Judea, and all ye that dwell at Jerusalem”. “For these are not drunken, as ye suppose, seeing it is but the third hour of the day.” That’s 9:00 a.m. Simon Peter gets up and lets them know these men ain’t drunk.

“But this is that which was spoken by the prophet Joel”. This is the prophet Joel coming to pass: “I will pour out of my Spirit upon all flesh”, down to “whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be saved.”
“Ye men of Israel, hear these words”. Peter tells you who the whosoever is: the men of Israel. “Jesus of Nazareth, a man approved of God among you by miracles and wonders and signs”.
“Ye have taken, and by wicked hands have crucified and slain”.

“Now when they heard this, they were pricked in their heart, and said unto Peter and to the rest of the apostles, Men and brethren, what shall we do?” Now they understand: we were looking for the Messiah the whole time, and we ended up killing him.
“Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost.”

“For the promise is unto you, and to your children, and to all that are afar off”. Who’s afar off? The Israelites. “Even as many as the Lord our God shall call.” Who is called? The Israelites.

So we understand who the book of Acts is written to, what Christ’s doctrine is, and what the apostles’ doctrine is.

“God that made the world and all things therein”. Who is that? Our foundation, Jesus Christ; he made all things. “Seeing that he is Lord of heaven and earth, dwelleth not in temples made with hands”, and he “giveth to all life, and breath, and all things”. Our God created everything.

This one is for all the apologetics out there. “And hath made of one blood all nations of men for to dwell on all the face of the earth”. They would say that’s talking about everybody. So you mean to tell me we went through all of that, Acts 1, Acts 2, Christ’s ministry and who it was for, and now we get to Acts 17 and everything changes? The hell is this?

They always talk about context, so read from verse 24. Common sense will tell you that if it’s talking about one thing, it’s not just going to change. It’s your duty to search the scriptures and get the understanding.

All nations of men: we already know we’ve been scattered in all nations. “And hath determined the times before appointed, and the bounds of their habitation”: how long they will be here.

“That they should seek the Lord, if haply they might feel after him, and find him, though he be not far from every one of us”. Who’s the they? All nations of men. Who’s the us? Who’s the they? It’s the Israelites. Christ is our foundation, and he is not far from us.

“For we are also his offspring.” “Forasmuch then as we are the offspring of God, we ought not to think that the Godhead is like unto gold, or silver, or stone, graven by art and man’s device.” Who’s the offspring? Israel is the offspring. So “hath made of one blood all nations of men”: those men have to be talking about ye men of Israel.
“And the times of this ignorance God winked at”. In the times of idolatry, when we went off, God winked at that. “But now commandeth all men every where to repent”.

precepts.why:
“Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost”.

Christ commanded the twelve to go out and teach all nations. Why? Because Israel was scattered among them.

“Confess him before the Gentiles, ye children of Israel: for he hath scattered us among them.”

Confess him before the other nations, ye children of Israel, for he hath scattered us among them. That is why the apostles were sent to all nations, and why Acts 17:26 speaks of all nations of men.

All nations of men: “James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad, greeting.”

We’ve been scattered all throughout, throughout all nations.

“Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia”.

That’s five nations right there. Those strangers, as we already read earlier, are Israelites, scattered among the nations.

The bounds of their habitation: how long they’ll be here. “Seeing his days are determined, the number of his months are with thee, thou hast appointed his bounds that he cannot pass”.

God created man, and he is superior to man. He determines the bounds that man cannot pass.

“Of his own will begat he us with the word of truth, that we should be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures.”

Christ is the first fruits. We’re a kind of first fruits, because he created us. But we’ve got limitations: he has appointed our bounds.

Though he be not far from every one of us. “For this commandment which I command thee this day, it is not hidden from thee, neither is it far off.”

“It is not in heaven, that thou shouldest say, Who shall go up for us to heaven, and bring it unto us, that we may hear it, and do it? Neither is it beyond the sea”. “But the word is very nigh unto thee”. Christ is very nigh unto thee. Who’s the thee in Deuteronomy? The Israelites.

So the us of Acts 17:27, from whom he is not far, is Israel.

Remember the strangers of Rome; we know who that is talking about. “Say not in thine heart, Who shall ascend into heaven? (that is, to bring Christ down from above:)” That is seeking the Lord: where is he, how are we going to find him?

“But what saith it? The word is nigh thee, even in thy mouth, and in thy heart”. Christ is nigh unto us. He is not afar off anymore. Now through Christ we are brought back into the fold.

“That if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved.” Who is that salvation for?

Who is that salvation for? “Him hath God exalted with his right hand to be a Prince and a Saviour, for to give repentance to Israel, and forgiveness of sins.”

To give repentance to Israel. Salvation, repentance, forgiveness of sins: they are for the nation of Israel. So the they that seek the Lord, and the us that he is not far from, in Acts 17:27, are Israel.

We need to figure out what that offspring is talking about. “Yet now hear, O Jacob my servant; and Israel, whom I have chosen: Thus saith the Lord that made thee, and formed thee from the womb, which will help thee; Fear not, O Jacob, my servant; and thou, Jesurun, whom I have chosen.”

“For I will pour water upon him that is thirsty, and floods upon the dry ground: I will pour my spirit upon thy seed, and my blessing upon thine offspring”.

You see that? Israel, Jacob, is the offspring of God. So “we are the offspring of God” in Acts 17:29 is Israel, and the all nations of men made of one blood are the men of Israel.

sense.text:
“And they are informed of thee, that thou teachest all the Jews which are among the Gentiles”. Do you see it? All the Jews, among the Gentiles. Why? Because we were scattered amongst all nations.

“To forsake Moses, saying that they ought not to circumcise their children, neither to walk after the customs.” That was the lie they were accusing the Apostle Paul of.
“The Jews which were of Asia, when they saw him in the temple, stirred up all the people, and laid hands on him”.

“Crying out, Men of Israel, help: This is the man, that teacheth all men every where against the people, and the law, and this place”.

“And further brought Greeks also into the temple, and hath polluted this holy place.” Those Greeks were Hellenized Jews, Greek-speaking Jews. Greeks and Grecians are to be distinguished: Grecians were Greek-speaking Jews.

So this has been the acts of the apostles and foundation through Christ, so that when you open up the book of Acts, you can actually understand what it’s talking about.
